newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Landmark ban on chemical weapons to enter into force.
newsitem.headline: Landmark ban on chemical weapons to enter into force.

text.p: A landmark convention banning the development, production, stockpiling and use of chemical weapons will enter into force on April 29, 1997, after Hungary became the 65th country to ratify the accord, a U.N. spokesman said on Thursday.

The Chemical Weapons Convention was opened for signature in Paris by Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali in January 1993. It was the result of a decade of negotiations in the Conference on Disarmament, the international community's main disarmament negotiating body.
It comes into force 180 days after the United Nations received the 65th ratification.
A technical secretariat headquartered at The Hague will be responsible for verifying its provisions are carried out.
Each state party undertakes to destroy chemical weapons and such production facilities it owns.
The official name of the accord is the Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production, Stockpiling and Use of Chemical Weapons and on their Destruction.
